facts.raw_span: a 1-year history of pain and swelling around his right ankle
bony thickening over the lateral malleolus
the ankle and subtalar joints had a full range of motion
Complete blood count was within normal limits
erythrocyte sedimentation rate was 68 mm at the first hour
a submetaphyseal lytic lesion in the distal tibia with a well-defined sclerotic margin
a diagnosis of Brodie’s abscess was made
curettage was performed under spinal anesthesia via an anterior approach
curetted material was sent for histopathological and microbiological assessment

concepts.why: The patient's 1-year history of pain and swelling around the ankle, bony thickening, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and radiographic findings of a submetaphyseal lytic lesion with a sclerotic margin support the diagnosis of Brodie's abscess.
The patient's long-standing symptoms, elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and radiographic findings suggest a chronic infection of the bone, which is consistent with chronic osteomyelitis.
The patient's symptoms and radiographic findings are consistent with a subacute infection of the bone, which is a possible diagnosis given the clinical presentation.

The radiographic finding of a submetaphyseal lytic lesion with a sclerotic margin could be consistent with a bone cyst, although the clinical context and other findings suggest that this is less likely.
The patient's symptoms and radiographic findings could be consistent with a bone tumor such as Ewing's sarcoma, although the clinical context and other findings suggest that this is less likely.
The patient's symptoms and radiographic findings could be consistent with an osteoid osteoma, although the clinical context and other findings suggest that this is less likely.
